a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: The query is antipyrine, a small neutral N-phenyl pyrazolone; the closest L5 analog edaravone showed very high Caco-2/MDCK permeability (Papp >10×10^-6 cm/s) and no P-gp efflux (efflux ratio <1, unchanged by verapamil), indicating no gut-wall efflux limitation.

Other L5 small neutral/heteroaromatic records show high passive permeability and efflux ratios near 1 (diazepam 55×10^-6 cm/s, phenobarbital 34×10^-6 cm/s both directions, warfarin ER 0.4-1.0, aspirin ER <1.5, compound 28 ER 0.97, compound 32 ER 0.86, TAK-063 ER 1.1), supporting unimpaired intestinal permeation for this compound class.

L1 human F values for structurally related N-aryl azolones/azoles and small heteroaromatic drugs are 52-87%, including fed-state values of 59-65% (eltrombopag 52%, teneligliptin 75-87%, trazodone 63-65% after food, ziprasidone 59-60% fed, urapidil 69-78%), supporting F >= 20%.

L4 absorption records show the closest structural analog phenylbutazone is rapidly and completely absorbed in humans, and many small neutral/high-permeability drugs have complete or high human absorption (diazepam 97-100%, ketoprofen 85-100%, nefazodone complete, methaqualone readily absorbed, TAK-063 highly permeable).

No L5 or earlier card provides affirmative evidence of gut-wall efflux, intestinal metabolism, or F < 20% for the query or a close analog; low-F records for TFMPP, brexanolone, and mCPP are structurally dissimilar or condition-mismatched and do not support a low prediction.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental absolute oral bioavailability value for antipyrine is present in the supplied cards.
No fed-state-specific antipyrine F or absorption measurement is available.
L5 gut-wall efflux/intestinal-metabolism records are for analogs (closest: edaravone) rather than the query; transfer is qualitative.
No matched oral-versus-IV exposure record for antipyrine is supplied.
No direct intestinal metabolism assay for antipyrine is supplied.
